single_nq_dev_2764
the kinked demand curve in oligopoly is used to explain
A: ["Kinked demand", "Kinked demand", "Kinked demand", "Oligopoly", "Oligopoly", "Kinked demand"]
Q: the kinked demand curve in oligopoly is used to explain
A: "The kinked demand curve in oligopoly is used to explain sticky prices and the behavior of firms in an oligopolistic market. It illustrates how firms may not change their prices in response to changes in demand or costs due to the anticipated reactions of competitors, leading to price rigidity. The curve features a concave bend, indicating that firms face different elasticities of demand above and below the kink, which results in a discontinuity in the marginal revenue curve. This model helps to understand why prices in oligopolistic markets tend to remain stable despite changes in market conditions."
A: The kinked demand curve in oligopoly is used to explain sticky prices and the behavior of firms in an oligopolistic market. It illustrates how firms may not change their prices in response to changes in demand or costs due to the anticipated reactions of competitors, leading to price rigidity. The curve features a concave bend, indicating that firms face different elasticities of demand above and below the kink, which results in a discontinuity in the marginal revenue curve. This model helps to understand why prices in oligopolistic markets tend to remain stable despite changes in market conditions

single_nq_dev_5797
why do longer dna molecules move more slowly than shorter ones during electrophoresis
A: ["Gel electrophoresis", "Agarose gel electrophoresis", "Agarose gel electrophoresis", "Agarose gel electrophoresis", "Agarose gel electrophoresis", "Gel electrophoresis of nucleic acids"]
Q: why do longer dna molecules move more slowly than shorter ones during electrophoresis
A: "Longer DNA molecules move more slowly than shorter ones during electrophoresis because they encounter more resistance as they navigate through the pores of the gel matrix. The gel acts as a sieving medium, and shorter molecules can migrate more easily through these pores, allowing them to travel faster. In contrast, longer molecules have a greater surface area and are more hindered by the gel's structure, which slows their movement. This phenomenon is often referred to as sieving, where the size of the DNA fragments determines their rate of migration through the gel."
A: Longer DNA molecules move more slowly than shorter ones during electrophoresis because they encounter more resistance as they navigate through the pores of the gel matrix. Q: why group 2 elements called alkaline earth metals
A: "Group 2 elements are called alkaline earth metals because they share certain chemical properties that are characteristic of both alkaline metals and earth metals. The term \"alkaline\" refers to the basic (alkaline) nature of the hydroxides formed when these metals react with water, producing alkaline solutions. The term \"earth\" historically referred to the oxides of these metals, which were found in nature as insoluble compounds. Early chemists believed these oxides were the fundamental components of the earth, hence the name \"earth metals.\" Together, these characteristics led to the designation of these elements as alkaline earth metals."
